item: Lane D2 duplicate hunt (mcp-refresh-audit 2026-09-19, post-restart): cross-surface duplicate detection for gemini/zcode/hermes/claude vs the .agents registry, plus the -hub twins. All config reads were read-only; no writes, no commits.

steps.detail: Registry 92 servers (targets histogram: claude 79, hermes 17, zcode 15, codex 9, gemini 5). Claude root mcpServers 87, per-project mcpServers 0. Gemini settings.json mcpServers 31. McpHub children 65 (all enabled=true, 0 disabled). Hermes config.yaml mcp_servers 17. zcode cli config mcp.servers 2 (exa, kaggle).

steps.action: FINDING D2-1: McpHub children vs direct mounts - 57 dual-mount pairs on the SAME consumer surface (claude)
steps.detail: 57 of 65 McpHub children have a same-named DIRECT mount in claude root mcpServers, i.e. one claude session can load the same server via both paths. Classification after cmd-wrapper unwrap + slash normalization: 44 byte-identical launches; 6 identical modulo path style (claude.json uses forward slashes, .McpHub backslashes: apktool-mcp, jadx-mcp, ocr-suite, openmm-md, qdx-rush, schrodinger); 5 TRANSPORT-DIVERGENT - claude mounts the CyberStrike HTTP hub while McpHub spawns the same server stdio (cloud-audit 127.0.0.1:31118, cve-mcp :31111, github-security :31110, nuclei :31117, osint :31112); 2 LAUNCHER-DIVERGENT (scholarly-access: scholarly-access-mcp.exe vs python -m scholarly_access.server, same venv; rdkit: rdkit_mcp_launch.py vs run_server.py --transport stdio, same venv). All 65 children enabled=true, so all 57 pairs are live double-spawn candidates. 8 children have NO direct mount (biomni-hub, everything, fb-messenger, insta-mcp, markitdown, meta-tool, sliver, tiktok). Second signal (mechanically independent of config reads - this session's own live tool inventory): both families connected simultaneously, e.g. mcp__social_hub__fb_dm_list AND mcp__McpHub__social_hub__fb_dm_list, likewise schrodinger, osint, mitmproxy, searxng, github-security, cloud-audit, playwright-cdp, playwright-extension, claude-code-mcp, paper-search - the duplicate is active, not theoretical; each connected pair doubles that server's tool-schema context cost.
steps.target: C:\Users\Prekzursil\.McpHub\config.json (servers) vs C:\Users\Prekzursil\.claude.json (mcpServers); McpHub mounted as entry 'McpHub' type sse http://127.0.0.1:24680/mcp
steps.risk: HIGH bloat: up to 57 double spawns / duplicated tool inventories per session; conflicting pins impossible today (PIN-DRIFT between twin sides = 0) but any future one-sided edit silently diverges the two paths

steps.action: FINDING D2-2: registry URL-twin pairs (the -hub twins)
steps.detail: 6 pairs in agents.json mcp.servers point at ONE URL each: github-security[claude]/github-security-hub[hermes] @ http://127.0.0.1:31110/mcp; cve-mcp/cve-mcp-hub @ :31111; osint/osint-hub @ :31112; firecrawl[claude,hermes]/firecrawl-kit[codex,claude] @ :31114; nuclei/nuclei-hub @ :31117; cloud-audit/cloud-audit-hub @ :31118. Five pairs are intentional per-consumer aliases (hermes is the HTTP-hub-only consumer; hermes config.yaml carries exactly the -hub URLs and its 17-server set equals the registry hermes-targeted set exactly). The exception is firecrawl vs firecrawl-kit: BOTH target claude on the same URL - only enabled=false on firecrawl-kit prevents a live same-surface duplicate; one enable flip (or a sync that materializes targeted-but-absent entries) creates it.
steps.target: C:\Users\Prekzursil\.agents\agents.json mcp.servers entries quoted: github-security url=http://127.0.0.1:31110/mcp targets=[claude] enabled=True ; github-security-hub same url targets=[hermes] enabled=True ; firecrawl targets=[claude,hermes] enabled=True ; firecrawl-kit targets=[codex,claude] enabled=False ; (same pattern for cve-mcp/osint/nuclei/cloud-audit pairs)
steps.risk: MEDIUM: firecrawl-kit is a latent same-surface duplicate for claude; the 6 alias pairs also bloat the SSOT and can confuse any consumer that ignores targets

steps.detail: Within-surface identical-identity duplicates: claude root 0, gemini 0, McpHub children 0, registry 6 (the URL pairs above). Package-level overlaps that are NOT same-server: playwright-cdp + playwright-extension share npm:@playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (two configs of one package - and the pair exists BOTH as claude direct mounts AND as McpHub children = 4 launches of the same pinned package on one surface); postgres + sonarqube share command 'docker' (different containers - not duplicates).
steps.risk: LOW-MEDIUM: playwright quadruple-mount is pure context-cost when all connect

steps.action: Gemini surface vs claude vs registry (31 entries)
steps.detail: 0 internal duplicates; all 31 names exist in the registry and on the claude surface (cross-surface overlap is expected, not flagged). Governance gap rather than duplication: only 5 registry entries target gemini (context7, github_cli, huggingface, linear, notion) - the other 26 gemini-mounted servers (binary-ninja-mcp, browserstack, cheatengine, chrome-devtools, codacy, codecov, deepsource, digitalocean, docker, excel, figma, firecrawl, frida-mcp, ghidra-mcp, hexstrike-ai, ida-pro-mcp, mcp-graphql, pdf-reader, playwright, ralph-orchestrator, repomix, scrapegraph, semgrep, sentry, sonarqube, tavily) are governed by name only, not by target - no sync path updates them.
steps.risk: MEDIUM: 26/31 gemini servers drift silently (freshness is lane A, but the governance hole is structural)

steps.detail: Live zcode MCP surface is 2 servers in .zcode\cli\config.json mcp.servers: exa (url https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp) and kaggle (stdio: C:\Users\Prekzursil\Downloads\bionlp\.venv\Scripts\python.exe + script). Registry declares 15 zcode-targeted entries (agent-mail, basic-memory, bedrock-claude, biomni-hub, burp, deepwiki, exa, github, kaggle, openaiDeveloperDocs, scholarly-access, video-agent-kit, web-reader, web-search-prime, zread) - 13 of 15 never materialize in the zcode config. UNVERIFIED whether zcode consumes the registry at runtime; settling experiment: run zcode's MCP-listing command (or check its docs) and see whether the 13 appear. Config-quality note: the kaggle entry points into a Downloads\bionlp venv - fragile location.
steps.risk: LOW duplication risk (2 servers, no internal dupes); MEDIUM governance mismatch (registry targets vs live config)

steps.action: hermes vs registry - includes CORRECTION to this morning's audit artifact
steps.detail: Hermes MCP config EXISTS at AppData\Local\hermes\config.yaml with mcp_servers: 17 entries, and the set equals the registry hermes-targeted set exactly (both directions verified: only-in-yaml=[], only-in-registry=[]). 0 duplicates, 0 ungoverned extras. CORRECTION: harness-audits/2026-09-19-mcp-tui-audit/tui-inventory.json records hermes as found:[] / mcp_servers:null and zcode likewise - that probe under-searched (missed AppData\Local\hermes and .zcode\cli\config.json's 'mcp' key shape); both surfaces are real and measured here.
steps.risk: none for duplication; the morning artifact's zcode/hermes rows should not be cited as 'no MCP config'

steps.action: Claude surface ungoverned extras and registry->claude gaps
steps.detail: 16 claude-root names absent from the registry: McpHub, apktool-mcp, codex, elevenlabs, gitlab, jadx-mcp, mcp-windbg, ocr-suite, openmm-md, perplexity, qdx-rush, rdkit, schrodinger, searxng, serena, zai-mcp-server. 14 of these are ALSO McpHub children (i.e. they participate in D2-1 dual mounts while ungoverned); zai-mcp-server is ungoverned and hub-less. Registry entries targeted claude but absent from claude root (8): firecrawl-kit (disabled), glm53-space, hacktricks, libgen, markitdown, meta-tool, metasploit, sliver-full - markitdown/meta-tool/sliver materialize only as McpHub children. Same-name claude-vs-registry identity drift: 0 (live mounts are faithful to the SSOT wherever the name exists).
steps.risk: MEDIUM: ungoverned dual-mounted entries escape both SSOT review and sync

steps.action: Collapse a false twin: the two McpHub config paths are ONE file
steps.detail: C:\Users\Prekzursil\.mcphub\config.json and C:\Users\Prekzursil\.McpHub\config.json are the same filesystem object (Windows case-insensitive paths; os.path.samefile=True, identical st_ino, identical size 13827 and mtime; 65/65 names, 0 content differences). There is exactly ONE McpHub child config, not two.
steps.risk: none (removes a phantom from the audit surface list)

steps.detail: First identity pass collapsed all 'cmd /c ...' Windows wrappers into one 'path:cmd' bucket, producing absurd 23-name match groups (the collection-level-equality tell). Fixed by unwrapping cmd/powershell wrappers, correcting uvx package resolution (--from value / first positional), stripping pip ==pins, and normalizing backslash/forward-slash + env expansion. All numbers reported here come from the corrected pass; the fix was validated against known pairs (social-hub, playwright-cdp became exact matches).
steps.target: extraction scripts at C:\Users\Prekzursil\AppData\Local\Temp\d2_extract*.py (scratch, read-only audit helpers)
steps.risk: none residual known; slash-style differences were the last false-drift source and are now normalized

Morning-audit correction: tui-inventory.json rows 'zcode: found[]/mcp_servers:null' and 'hermes: found[]/mcp_servers:null' are under-probes; both surfaces exist (paths above) and are fully measured in this lane
open_questions: Does zcode consume the .agents registry at runtime (13 of 15 zcode-targeted registry entries absent from its own config)? Settle by running zcode's MCP-list command or reading its loader docs.
Is the rdkit dual entrypoint intentional (rdkit_mcp_launch.py vs run_server.py --transport stdio in the same venv)? If not, one side is stale.

Owner decision (recommendation only, no action taken): prune the 57 dual mounts to ONE path per server (direct mount OR McpHub child) - today they are consistent (pin drift 0) but any one-sided edit silently diverges them; the playwright package is mounted 4x on one surface.
firecrawl-kit (enabled=false, targets codex+claude, same URL as firecrawl): confirm it stays disabled or loses the claude target, otherwise it is one enable-flip from a live same-surface duplicate.
npm/PyPI upstream freshness for the quoted pins was NOT checked in this lane (belongs to the version-freshness lane A); all pin claims here are config-side only.
